subject: Re: Vendor replacement economics — Redwood vs SolNet (pricing + packaging)
messages:
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmesys.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmesys.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 16:14:00 -0800
Subject: Replacement & pricing: Redwood evaluation vs SolNet

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the call this morning. To move Acme forward we need a clear side-by-side of total first-year economics, and a realistic replacement plan from SolNet (our incumbent) to Redwood. Procurement pushed back on an initial high-level number — they asked for:

- 12-month committed pricing with unit rates by token and per-embedding call
- Any onboarding/ingestion credits you can provide
- Packaging differences (hosted vs. dedicated) and what we’d need to change on our side

Attached is the SolNet commercial summary they shared with us (redacted). Can you send a competitive match and a short migration checklist we can give to our infra team?

We’re on a pretty compressed timeline: procurement wants a signed decision by 2026-12-15 to qualify for year-end budget.

Appreciate your help — Tom

--
Tom Rivera
Head of Cloud Procurement
Acme Systems
T: 415-555-0123
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmesys.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Replacement & pricing: Redwood evaluation vs SolNet

Tom — thanks for the context and the timeline. I’ve put together a compact comparison and two commercial options attached (redwood_acme_competitive_sheet.xlsx) plus a draft SOW for the recommended path (SOW-draft-v1.pdf). High-level summary below:

Option A — Hosted, 12-month commit (fastest cutover)
- 12-month committed spend: $240k
- Effective token rate (est.): $0.0009/token (based on your traffic profile)
- Onboarding credit: $25k (one-time)
- Support: Standard + 24/7 incident playbook during cutover

Option B — Dedicated reserved pool (recommended for predictable latency)
- 12-month reserved capacity: $320k
- Lower marginal token rate: $0.0006/token after commit
- Migration support included (2 weeks remote eng + 1 week onsite optional)
- One-time onboarding credit: $40k

Key migration notes (short checklist for infra):
- Network: VPC peering + IP allowlist (1–2 days config)
- Data: optional customer-managed KMS for keys (if required)
- Model parity: we’ll provide model versioning and test prompts for quality gating
- Cutover: can do staged routing (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over 48–72 hours

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm preferred option (Hosted vs Dedicated)
2) I’ll loop in Finance for a final pricing letter if you want a formal match
3) If procurement agrees, we’ll issue a revised SOW + DocuSign link this week

Looping in Monica (Finance) and Marcus (Solutions) to weigh in on pricing levers and any operational constraints.

– Laura

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 646-555-0098

Attachments: redwood_acme_competitive_sheet.xlsx; SOW-draft-v1.pdf

Laura — thanks, this is helpful. A few quick datapoints from procurement & infra:

- SolNet is offering a blended effective token rate at $0.00075 with a 12-month commit and a $50k migration credit.
- They require a 60-day notification for the committed pool change (we can meet that)
- Infra asked about cache migration: is there an expected delta in latency during the first 48 hours?

Procurement’s ask: can Redwood get within ~5–7% of SolNet’s effective token rate and match a $50k onboarding credit? If you can do that, we’ll fast-track the paperwork.

Can you and your team confirm the latency/caching risk and if you can improve the credit/price?

Thanks — Tom

Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Replacement & pricing: Redwood evaluation vs SolNet

All — quick internal calc and recommendation from Finance:

1) Pricing match: We can bring Option A (Hosted) to an effective $0.00078/token with a $45k onboarding credit if Acme commits to 12 months and a minimum monthly committed spend of $20k. That gets us within ~4% of SolNet’s blended rate.

2) Dedicated alternative: If Acme picks Dedicated and commits $300k/yr, we can do $0.00055/token with a $50k onboarding credit, plus one month free reserved capacity (to help with cache warm-up).

3) Latency/caching note: Marcus — can you confirm feasibility of the 48-hour warm-up window and whether the one-month free reserved capacity is sufficient to avoid regressions? We should capture a short SLA addendum for cache-related incidents during the first 30 days.

If Marcus confirms, I recommend pushing the Dedicated package (better long-term economics) while offering a bridged Hosted offer (0.00078/token + $45k credit) so procurement has a quick path to sign. I’ve attached a simple workbook (pricing_note_monica.xlsx) with the blended math.

— Monica

Tom — quick update following internal review:

Offer (final, commercial):
- Hosted bridge (12 months): effective $0.00078/token, $45k onboarding credit, standard SLA; cutover playbook included.
- Dedicated preferred (12 months): $300k reserved, $0.00055/token, $50k onboarding credit, plus one month free reserved capacity to help warm caches. Includes a 30-day cache incident addendum.

Marcus validated the warm-up plan (staged ramp + pre-warm tooling) and believes the one-month free reserved capacity should eliminate meaningful latency regressions during the transition. Monica confirmed the finance math.

I’ve attached the updated SOW (SOW-final-acme.pdf). If this matches what procurement needs, we’ll send a DocuSign link and aim to complete signature by 2026-12-10 to respect your timeline.

Would you like us to send the DocuSign now or wait until you’ve reviewed with procurement?

Best — Laura
